title: Census retail and wholesale benchmark revision — the NOT-adjusted restatement on the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey
source: EST: census.gov/mtis/index.html announcements block, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 684,348 bytes), verbatim: "Intention to Revise - Monthly retail and monthly wholesale estimates are anticipated to be revised based on historical corrections and the results of the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey. Revised not adjusted estimates and corresponding adjusted estimates are tentatively scheduled for release on September 28, 2026 and October 26, 2026, respectively. Revisions to the retail estimates are anticipated to be reflected in the August 2026 MTIS release scheduled for October 15, 2026. Revisions to the wholesale estimates are anticipated to be reflected in the September 2026 MTIS release scheduled for November 17, 2026." ONE primary only, and Census's own word is "tentatively". Filed estimate on both counts — the lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the mtis-2026-12-16 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). It is the FIRST of a two-step benchmark, and only the second step is on this calendar: the sibling wholesale lane proposed mwts-benchmark-revision-2026-10-26 from the census.gov/wholesale announcements block, which names the 10-26 SEASONALLY ADJUSTED release alone. The MTIS block quoted above names both halves and dates the NOT-adjusted release 2026-09-28, four weeks earlier and TWENTY-TWO DAYS from this proposal — by a wide margin the nearest untracked dated item this sweep found. Read the two proposals as one revision in two publications, not as duplicates; if a later session judges them a single event, this is the earlier date and the one that arrives first. Why it belongs on the calendar: it restates the retail and wholesale levels that two thirds of every MTIS aggregate is built from, and Census dates the downstream effect precisely — retail restated into the 2026-10-15 MTIS edition, wholesale into the 2026-11-17 edition. So every level, ratio and percentile written about this family before those dates is pre-revision arithmetic, and mtis-2026-12-16 is the first October-reference edition standing on the restated basis for two of its three legs while a separate Special Notice on the same page freezes the third (M3 historical data and seasonal adjustment models unchanged for the remainder of 2026). Impact LOW, symbols empty: a benchmark restatement of a series with no macro-keyed playbook and no instrument attached. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry, and a revision to history is explicitly not a signal about the future.
